data.title: US Stocks Edge Up On Short Trading Day
data.description:
US stocks rose but pared initial gains during a holiday-shortened trading day as tech stocks looked to recover amid a volatile November.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 0.6%. The S&P 500 gained 0.7%. The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite jumped 0.8% after markets were closed for the Thanksgiving holiday.

Semiconductor stocks rebounded as investors’ nerves over AI profitability eased and a sell-off in tech took a breather. Nvidia shares fell 2% in early trading after opening in the green, while Micron stock rose 2%.Crude oil prices rose, with global benchmark Brent crude climbing to $91 per barrel, after Houthi militants ramped up attacks against energy infrastructure in Saudi Arabia.

Treasury yields, meanwhile, continued to fall after third quarter US GDP rose 4.3%, indicating that the economy is booming. The 10-year yield was little changed at 4.89%.

The stock market will close early on Friday at 1 p.m. ET, and the bond market will close at 2 p.m., with no major earnings or economic data releases on the calendar.

Yahoo Finance

data.title: Tokyo Stock Market Jumps On Bargain Hunting
data.description:
Tokyo stocks ended higher Friday as investors went bargain hunting following the market’s recent declines.

The benchmark Nikkei stock index, the 225-issue Nikkei Stock Average, rose 1,211.95 points, or 2.11 percent, from Thursday to close at 58,711.11.

The broader Topix index, meanwhile, finished 64.80 points, or 1.73 percent, higher at 3,815.20.

Dip-buying and reinvestment following interim dividend payments supported the market after its recent slide, analysts said, adding that with concerns over artificial intelligence- and chip-related stocks lingering, the market’s upside is likely to remain limited.

data.title: Chinese Stocks Surge As Shanghai Composite Reclaims 3,600 Points, Tech Leads
data.description:
Chinese equities surged during Friday’s afternoon trading session, with major stock indexes posting sharp gains as technology and growth stocks led a broad market rally.

The benchmark Shanghai Composite Index climbed 3.5% as of 2pm, briefly reclaiming the psychologically significant 3,600-point level.

Meanwhile, the Shenzhen Component Index jumped 6.7%, outperforming the Shanghai benchmark amid strong gains in growth-oriented equities.

The ChiNext Index, which tracks companies listed on China’s Nasdaq-style growth enterprise board, surged more than 10%, reflecting particularly strong buying interest in growth stocks.

The STAR Composite Index, which measures the performance of companies on Shanghai’s science and technology innovation board, recorded an even sharper increase of 13%.

The substantial gains across technology-focused indexes highlighted their leadership in the afternoon rally, with both outperforming China’s broader equity benchmarks.

The advance also signalled improved market sentiment, although the extent to which the gains could be sustained remained uncertain.

The Shanghai Composite’s return above 3,600 points marked a notable intraday recovery for the benchmark, while the stronger performances of the Shenzhen, ChiNext and STAR indexes underscored the momentum in technology and innovation-related shares.

The figures represented market movements as of 2pm local time, ahead of the close of Friday’s trading session.

data.title: Gold Stages 2.1% Comeback, Yet RHB Sees More Room To Fall
data.description:
Gold prices rebounded on Friday, recovering from a more-than-one-year low as easing jitters over technology stocks reduced selling pressure, although RHB Research maintained its bearish outlook on the precious metal.

Spot gold rose 2.1% to US$3,640.84 an ounce by 2.09pm Malaysian time, after hitting its lowest level since August 2025 on Wednesday. US gold futures for December delivery gained 3% to US$3,640.20.

Bullion was up about 3.1% for the week, while silver climbed 6% to US$43.96 an ounce. Platinum and palladium also advanced, gaining 4.3% each.

VT Markets chief strategy officer Ross Maxwell said the US Thanksgiving holiday lull had eased selling pressure as the selloff in technology stocks and asset liquidations paused.

However, he said the timing of a sustained recovery would depend on movements in real interest rates, the US dollar and investment flows.

RHB Research, meanwhile, retained its short positions on COMEX Gold, saying the technical setup remained bearish despite the commodity recovering above the US$3,500 support level.

The research house said COMEX Gold had rebounded from an intraday low of US$3,425.20 on Wednesday to close at US$3,535.80, keeping the immediate support at US$3,500 intact.

It said the metal could attempt to test resistance at US$3,750 as long as it holds above the support level, but the downward trend in its 20-day and 50-day simple moving averages continued to exert pressure.

RHB Research maintained its recommendation to keep short positions initiated at US$3,885.30, with a stop-loss at US$3,750.

It identified the next support at US$3,350 should gold fall below US$3,500, while further resistance stood at US$3,875.

Meanwhile, expectations of further US interest rate increases continued to weigh on bullion, as higher rates raise the opportunity cost of holding non-yielding assets.

data.title: Asian Shares Stabilise After Bruising November, Dollar Heads For Third Monthly Gain
data.description:
Asian shares edged higher on Friday as a holiday lull offered some respite from a bruising month, while the US dollar remained on track for its third consecutive monthly gain amid safe-haven demand and expectations of another Federal Reserve interest rate hike, Reuters reported.

MSCI’s broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan rose 0.5%, putting it 1.9% higher for the week, although it remained down 8.2% for November.

Japan’s Nikkei climbed 0.7%, bringing its weekly gains to 2.7% but leaving it down 8.4% for the month. South Korea’s benchmark index rallied 2%, while China’s blue-chip CSI300 slipped 0.2%.

US stock futures also advanced, with S&P 500 futures up 0.8% and Nasdaq futures gaining 1%, following the Thanksgiving holiday closure on Wall Street.

Market sentiment remained cautious amid uncertainty over the growth outlook for artificial intelligence and the direction of US interest rates.

Tech giant Nvidia remained a source of concern after S&P placed its credit rating on watch for a possible downgrade. The Financial Times also reported that the chipmaker had told manufacturing partners to stop shipping servers containing its chips to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia.

Meanwhile, the US dollar index rose 1.8% against its major peers this month to 103.8, putting it on course for a third consecutive monthly gain.

The currency has been supported by safe-haven flows amid the equity market selloff and expectations that the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates in December. Futures imply a 99% probability of a 25-basis-point increase, although expectations of a larger half-point hike have faded.

The euro was flat at US$1.0964, while the New Zealand dollar edged up 0.2% to US$0.5482 following final election results that left the country’s ruling coalition short of a parliamentary majority.

In the bond market, two-year US Treasury yields rose three basis points to 4.6705%, while benchmark 10-year yields gained four basis points to 4.8918%.

Oil prices, meanwhile, were heading for their first weekly gain in four weeks amid renewed concerns over supply disruptions. Brent crude futures slipped 0.4% to US$96.14 a barrel on Friday but remained up 3.9% for the week.

data.title: Bursa Sees Room To Climb As Global Tech Shares Rebound
data.description:
Bursa Malaysia is expected to extend its recovery on Friday following a volatile week, with easing concerns over potential US tariffs and a rebound in global technology and banking shares offering some support to market sentiment.

Apex Securities said the local market appeared to be finding a bottom, with the FBM KLCI recording gains in two of the past three trading sessions.

It expects the benchmark index to sustain its recovery, supported by improved sentiment following Wednesday’s artificial intelligence (AI)-led sell-off.

The research house said the easing of concerns over the scope of new US tariffs, alongside a broad-based rebound in global technology and banking shares, could provide near-term relief for Malaysian technology stocks and AI-related infrastructure players.

However, it cautioned that uncertainty surrounding tighter US export-licensing rules continued to weigh on the sector.

In the opening minutes of trade, the FBM KLCI slipped 4.01 points to 1,566.97.

Apex Securities added that the approaching end of the corporate earnings season and the phased expansion of the FBM KLCI from 30 to 50 constituents could create stock-specific trading opportunities even as the broader market consolidates.

Banking stocks weighed on the benchmark, with Hong Leong Bank falling 10 sen to RM21, AmBank declining 10 sen to RM6.60 and Maybank shedding six sen to RM10.18.

Tenaga Nasional lost eight sen to RM12.42, while 99 Speed Mart slipped seven sen to RM3.28.

Among actively traded counters, NexG Bina fell half a sen to three sen, Zetrix AI declined half a sen to 4.5 sen and Ingenieur shed half a sen to 2.5 sen.

Regional markets were mostly positive, with Japan’s Nikkei rising 0.3% to 57,688 and South Korea’s Kospi gaining 0.5% to 4,736.

China’s Shanghai Composite and CSI 300 were flat at 3,476 and 3,900 respectively, while Hong Kong’s Hang Seng advanced 0.2% to 22,263.

data.title: Dollar Nears Two-Year High As Markets Brace For More Fed Tightening
data.description:
The US dollar hovered near a 22-month high on Friday as concerns over artificial intelligence (AI) stock valuations kept investors cautious, while expectations of further Federal Reserve rate hikes continued to support the greenback.

The dollar index, which measures the US currency against a basket of six major peers, was steady at 103.81 in holiday-thinned trading, after touching 104.53 on Monday, its highest level since March 2025.

The index has gained about 5.7% so far this year, although it has given up most of its gains from earlier in the week and was broadly flat for the week.

Investors were watching equity markets for signs of whether the recent decline in AI-related stocks would stabilise, with the direction of the technology sector likely to influence demand for risk-sensitive currencies.

“All eyes are on whether the downtrend in AI-related stocks will turn around,” Mizuho analysts wrote in a client note.

The Australian dollar, which is sensitive to shifts in risk appetite, edged down to US$0.6631 after falling to a one-year low of US$0.6559 on Wednesday.

Meanwhile, expectations of tighter US monetary policy continued to underpin the dollar, with traders viewing a 25-basis-point rate hike at the Federal Reserve’s Dec 9 meeting as almost certain, according to CME Group’s FedWatch tool.

Stronger-than-expected US core personal consumption expenditures inflation in October, an upward revision to third-quarter gross domestic product and a Federal Reserve survey indicating continued economic growth and persistent inflation have also strengthened expectations of another rate increase around April.

“The USD looks to be on a stronger-for-longer path than previously expected,” NAB strategists wrote in a research report.

However, they added that the dollar’s rapid appreciation left limited room for further gains.

Against other major currencies, the US dollar edged up 0.1% to 159.355 yen and strengthened slightly to 0.83455 Swiss franc. The euro was little changed at US$1.0964, while sterling eased to US$1.3099.

Reuters

data.title: West Asia Tensions Keep Ringgit From Gaining Ground
data.description:
The ringgit opened flat against the US dollar on Friday as geopolitical tensions and global economic uncertainties continued to support demand for the greenback.

At 8am, the local currency stood at 4.1135/1200 against the US dollar, unchanged from Thursday’s close of 4.1135/1175.

Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said the foreign exchange market was expected to remain cautious amid ongoing tensions in West Asia and concerns over the global economic outlook.

He noted that Brent crude oil prices rose 2.07% to US$96.57 per barrel on Thursday, following a strike on a Saudi Arabian oil refinery in Jazan that temporarily halted some of its operations.

The conflict in West Asia continued to pose risks to fuel supplies, while markets had fully priced in a 25-basis-point increase in the US Federal Funds Rate at the Federal Reserve’s December meeting.

Mohd Afzanizam also pointed to concerns over excessive investment in artificial intelligence, alongside a hawkish stance by the US Congress and administration towards China, as factors contributing to demand for the US dollar.

“Besides that, there are concerns over excessive investment in artificial intelligence (AI), as well as a hawkish stance by the US Congress and administration towards China.

“Hence, we foresee the forex market will continue to remain guarded, which would result in higher demand for the US dollar,” he told Bernama.

He expects the ringgit to trade within a narrow range of RM4.10 to RM4.12 against the US dollar today.

Against other major currencies, the ringgit strengthened slightly against the euro to 4.5121/5192 from 4.5133/5177 and the British pound to 5.3912/3997 from 5.3924/3976.

It also edged higher against the Japanese yen to 2.5824/5866 from 2.5834/5860.

Against ASEAN currencies, the ringgit weakened against the Thai baht to 12.0825/1095 from 12.0712/0875 but was unchanged against the Singapore dollar at 3.1878/1931.

It also remained flat against the Philippine peso at 6.45/6.46 and the Indonesian rupiah at 224.0/224.4.

data.title: HSIF’s Brief Recovery Faces Another Test At 22,500
data.description:
Hang Seng Index Futures (HSIF) extended its losing streak to seven consecutive sessions, with RHB Investment Bank Bhd (RHB Research) maintaining its negative trading bias and advising traders to stay on short positions.

The futures contract closed at 22,201 points after opening at 21,938 points and moving between an intraday high of 22,546 points and a low of 21,691 points.

It subsequently fell another 84 points in evening trading to last trade at 22,117 points.

In its technical analysis, RHB Research said the latest candlestick formation, which featured a long upper shadow, indicated that the 22,500-point level remained an immediate resistance.

A breakout above this level could open the way for further gains towards 23,000 points. However, the research house said the bearish technical setup remained intact, with both the 20-day and 50-day simple moving average (SMA) lines continuing to trend downwards.

It added that sellers would retain the technical upper hand as long as the HSIF remained below the 23,000-point threshold.

RHB Research advised traders to maintain short positions initiated at 23,576 points, or at the close on Nov 13, with a stop-loss level set at 23,500 points to manage trading risks.

On the downside, immediate support is placed at 21,500 points, followed by 20,500 points. Resistance is seen at 22,500 points and 23,000 points.

data.title: Stock Picks: Ta Ann And CIMB Group
data.description:
RHB Investment Bank Bhd (RHB Research) has identified Ta Ann Holdings and CIMB Group Holdings as stocks to watch, with the former attempting to extend its rebound while the latter maintains a bullish technical setup.

In its technical analysis, RHB Research said Ta Ann was testing immediate resistance after recording a bullish candlestick, although a long upper shadow indicated strong selling pressure at RM5.20.

A breakout above this level could attract fresh buying interest and lift the counter towards the next resistance levels of RM5.50 and RM5.75.

However, a fall below the RM4.95 support would signal a bearish breakout and potentially resume its corrective movement.

Meanwhile, CIMB Group is poised to extend its upward momentum after breaking above the RM7.15 resistance on strong trading volume.

RHB Research said the counter had climbed above its 21-day simple moving average and formed a bullish candlestick, indicating that its positive technical setup remained intact.

The banking stock is now eyeing the next resistance levels of RM7.50 and RM7.80. However, a breach of the RM6.90 support would invalidate the bullish outlook.

data.title: Bursa Rally Cools As FBM KLCI Retreats From 1,581 Midday Level
data.description:
Bursa Malaysia pared most of its midday gains to close higher on Thursday, with the benchmark FBM KLCI adding 8.69 points or 0.56% to 1,570.98 after retreating from its morning session level of 1,581.17.

The benchmark index had climbed 18.88 points or 1.21% at midday, reaching an intraday high of 1,584.96. However, it subsequently gave up much of those gains to finish at 1,570.98, still above its opening level of 1,563.15.

The broader market also weakened in the afternoon, with the FBM70 falling 291.56 points or 1.82% to 15,768.93, reversing its midday gain of 0.63%.

The FBM Small Cap Index shed 187.05 points or 1.33% to 13,918.83, while the FBM ACE Index recorded the steepest decline, dropping 177.78 points or 3.83% to 4,461.11.

The FBM Emas slipped 14.24 points or 0.12% to 11,467.68, while the FBM100 edged down 4.35 points or 0.04% to 11,329.11.

Among sector indices, the Consumer Products and Services Index was among the few gainers, rising 3.02 points or 0.70% to 437.39. The Construction Index fell 8.02 points or 2.87% to 271.28, while the Energy Index lost 3.52 points or 0.48% to 732.08.

Nestle remained among the day’s strongest performers, gaining RM1.48 to RM95.60, while Batu Kawan added 98 sen to RM19.98. Carlsberg Brewery Malaysia rose 50 sen to RM13.06, followed by PPB Group, which gained 47 sen to RM8.89, and Kuala Lumpur Kepong, up 42 sen to RM21.48.

On the most actively traded list, Malayan Agriculture and General (MAG) remained unchanged at 16 sen, with 76.49 million shares traded.

CBHB fell 10.5 sen to 46 sen after recording 66.47 million shares in volume, while ZETRIX was unchanged at five sen with 62.90 million shares traded. Dagang NeXchange (DNEX) slipped half a sen to 41.5 sen, while BCG gained three sen to RM1.18.

The market data was recorded at 5pm on November 26, with prices delayed by 15 minutes.

data.title: Stock Today: Sunway Slips 1% Despite Stronger Property And Construction Profits
data.description:
Sunway Bhd shares fell nearly 1% on Thursday afternoon, trading lower following the group’s latest quarterly results, which showed a 7.1% year-on-year decline in third-quarter net profit despite stronger contributions from its property development and construction divisions.

As at 3.28pm, the stock was down 4 sen or 0.98% at RM4.06, compared with its last adjusted closing price of RM4.10. It opened at RM4.00 and traded between RM3.98 and RM4.13, with 2.32 million shares changing hands.

The share price movement came after Sunway reported a 7.1% decline in net profit to RM314 million for the third quarter ended Sept 30, 2026, from RM338 million a year earlier, although revenue rose 18% to RM3 billion.

Its property development division recorded a 45.5% increase in profit before tax to RM80.1 million, while the construction segment’s profit before tax grew 13.3% to RM137.5 million.

For the first nine months of 2026, Sunway achieved property sales of RM3.4 billion, putting it on track to meet its full-year target of RM4.2 billion. Its unbilled property sales stood at RM8.2 billion.

The construction division also secured RM9.8 billion in new contracts during the nine-month period, lifting its outstanding order book to a record RM12.45 billion.

The group’s healthcare segment recorded quarterly revenue of RM738.3 million and profit before tax of RM119.1 million.
